affectedCaseDecisions.science: Coding DNA 5′-ATG GAA … TTT TGA-3′ gives mRNA 5′-AUG GAA … UUU UGA-3′ and the displayed product Met–Glu–…–Phe, then stop. The ellipsis is explicitly many in-frame full codons, not a nucleotide or a full three-residue enzyme. GAA pairs antiparallel with 3′-CUU-5′, equivalent to 5′-UUC-3′. The material separately stipulates a complete longer enzyme and its metabolic function. Typical bacterial process coupling and nuclear eukaryotic transcription/processing/export followed by cytoplasmic translation are correct within the named model. Intron-free does not prohibit other RNA maturation. No omitted sequence or actual enzyme structure/function is inferred from three shown residues.
affectedCaseDecisions.operatorAndSource: The connected explanation exercises HE KC2024 Q1.1 basic GK/LK protein-biosynthesis scope: pro/euk transcription, mRNA, translation, ribosome and tRNA. Enzyme renewal applies a supplied function. It is a bounded case contribution, not the whole HE source clause or the complete canonical goal. The unchanged code-wheel obligation and other source duties stay separate.

positiveEssentialConditionsLiteral: Correct codon/product correspondence with the explicit omitted complete-codon region

affectedCaseDecisions.science: Reference coding GAA and W GAG both give Glu; V GAC gives Asp. ATG→AUG gives Met, TTC→UUC gives Phe, and TAA→UAA is stop. The same long, unchanged, in-frame omitted region is stated for all three complete genes. The assay uses equal amounts of full longer purified proteins under equal conditions. V 12±2 versus reference 100±4 supports strongly reduced tested activity; W 98±4 versus 100±4 supports no clear difference under the supplied spread. This is not proof of identical function or universal synonymous neutrality. A large functional effect of a conservative amino-acid replacement is possible in a stipulated model; no structural mechanism is invented.
affectedCaseDecisions.operatorAndSource: BY12 GA and EA B12 2.4 both require explanation of mutation effects on the function of the encoded protein. This case links a single supplied sequence change to controlled full-protein function data, so it contributes to that shared duty. It does not cover every mutation type, mutagenic cause, whole canonical ffef goal, EA oncogenesis or the separate PCR comparison.
affectedCaseDecisions.bilingualParity: Both languages say the omitted sequence is the same long region, keep it in mRNA/product shorthand, identify the full protein assay and distinguish a synonymous position from a universal functional claim.
affectedCaseDecisions.atomicity: Mutation-to-tested-protein-function reasoning is one bounded content competence. Deriving the displayed codons and using assay controls are evidence steps for that competence. This targeted case decision does not issue a native A ledger record.

positiveEssentialConditionsLiteral: Connect actual everyday solar UV exposure to the supplied DNA-damage/fixation hazard without deterministic disease inference
Compare all three material-backed options using explicit stated criteria and priorities
State and justify the action judgement, organisation tradeoff and conditional alternative
Reject heat as sufficient UV evidence and separate exposure ratios from individual mutation/disease probabilities
affectedCaseDecisions.science: Solar UV can damage DNA and can favour persistent mutation when damage is not correctly resolved; a UV exposure does not imply a fixed mutation, and a mutation does not imply disease. Shade, skin-covering clothing and changing outdoor timing have qualitative BfS support. Exposures A100/B25/C10 are declared fictional same-duration model data. Reduced warmth does not establish reduced UV; no individual disease risk or percentage health benefit follows from these exposure units.
affectedCaseDecisions.operatorAndSource: The sports-day situation is recognisable everyday exposure. A/B/C are feasible alternatives with equal participation and stated exposure, organisational cost and priority. The learner must distinguish comparison from action judgement, recommend C under the given priority, weigh organisation and name B if schedule change is impossible. Heat-proxy criticism and limits require reflection on the hazard beyond a repair explanation or minimum-number choice. This fulfils a bounded MV everyday reflection example and the genetic-environmental evaluation operation from ST. It does not close either complete original source goal.
affectedCaseDecisions.bilingualParity: Both languages carry identical feasibility, duration, exposures, criterion order, C recommendation, conditional B option, false heat-proxy premise and personal-risk limitation. Positive conditions require all of those operations.
affectedCaseDecisions.atomicity: One concrete material-based genetic-risk decision. The damage premise supplies the biological reason; comparing options, exposing a value priority and choosing exposure reduction form one judgement rather than unrelated learning routines.
affectedCaseDecisions.remaining: ST is explicitly Schuljahrgang10/Einführungsphase; no SekI stage equivalence or native stage correction is approved. Final ID/placement/applicability, source relation and native evidence are pending.

positiveEssentialConditionsLiteral: Link the named chemical environmental mutagenic hazard to supplied DNA damage and bounded fixation mechanism
Evaluate all options with exposure, safe access, time cost and the explicit priority; justify rather than merely name a choice
Correctly compare five-day central exposure sums60/10/55 without individual disease probabilities or unsupported error aggregation

affectedCaseDecisions.science: UBA supplies incomplete wood-combustion PAH/benzo(a)pyrene and particle-associated air measurements. IARC supplies aromatic-compound/PAH DNA adducts and the repair relationship. The case cautiously distinguishes possible lasting genetic change from certain mutation or disease. Five comparable daily central exposures yield A60/B10/C55. The ± values are not specified as standard errors or confidence intervals, so no new error aggregation, clinical threshold or disease probability is inferred. A and C spreads overlap; a visual screen has no supplied particle-filtering evidence. B remains substantially lower across the supplied spreads and is safely accessible by stipulation.
affectedCaseDecisions.operatorAndSource: This daily bus-stop context addresses an environmental genetic hazard with three reachable options, safe-access and time criteria, an explicit priority and a six-minute tradeoff. B is justified against all criteria; the learner must give exposure sums, evaluate the screen claim, request weather-specific measurements and reject absence of visible smoke or immediate symptoms as safety proof. Those demands perform the MV everyday reflection and ST environmental genetic-risk evaluation operators. Mechanism knowledge alone cannot pass. This is a bounded case contribution, not source-wide or personal-health clearance.
affectedCaseDecisions.bilingualParity: DE and EN preserve the named hazard, same exposure central values and spreads, five days, safe bus access, extra six minutes, missing filter and weather evidence, B judgement and limits. No deterministic mutation or clinical interpretation is introduced in either version.
affectedCaseDecisions.atomicity: One informed environmental-risk and protective-action judgement. The arithmetic, uncertainty and evidence limits support that judgement; they do not create an independent statistical-learning goal.
affectedCaseDecisions.remaining: No real environmental experiment, learner work, legal threshold, clinical prediction, performed host trial or native acceptance is evidenced. ST stage and all seven prototype ID/route/evidence bindings remain pending.
